summary: Patch sets formfield.initial for UUIDField in formfield_for_dbfield, but this does not address the reported bug (the to_field target `id` is editable=False, so it never gets a formfield in the inline/admin form) and introduces a regression by assigning the NOT_PROVIDED sentinel as initial when a UUIDField has no default. Wrong layer and incorrect approach.

issues.description: Does not resolve the issue. The failing UUIDField (`id`) is `editable=False`, so `formfield_for_dbfield`/`formfield()` produces no editable form field for it; the real bug is that the parent's callable default is not populated before the inline FK (`to_field='id'`) is resolved on save. Setting formfield.initial here never fires for the reported scenario.

Wrong abstraction/fix location. The bug is in model save / related-field population for inlines with a `to_field` pointing at a defaulted field, not in admin form-field construction. Special-casing UUIDField in formfield_for_dbfield is a brittle, symptom-level patch.

Regression risk: when a UUIDField has no default, `db_field.default` is `models.NOT_PROVIDED` (not callable), so `formfield.initial = NOT_PROVIDED` — a sentinel leaks into the form as the initial value, altering rendering/behavior for editable UUIDFields without defaults. Guard should check `default is not NOT_PROVIDED`.

Fix is narrowly special-cased to UUIDField rather than the general class of fields with callable defaults used as FK to_field targets, indicating overfitting to the reported field type instead of a principled fix.
Comment says 'Ensure default values are set for UUIDField' but does not explain why UUIDField specifically or the interaction with editable=False / to_field, leaving intent unclear.
